vo: Same task, same Bot. The only difference between these two results is one round of good feedback.
A Bot is fast, but it doesn't know what feels off. That part is still your eye, and your eye is the skill that matters now.
The whole method fits in four steps: idea, plan, build, and feedback.
Step one, the idea. Say it in one clear picture, not a pile of features. One sentence the Bot can see.
If you have no idea yet, collect references first. Real examples beat a vague wish every time.
Step two, the plan. Ask the Bot to split your idea into scenes, with a time for each one, and read it before anything gets built.
The first plan will look generic. So show it the real thing. A few screenshots of the real screens change the result immediately.
Step three, build. Let the Bot work on its own, and use that time to prepare, not to interrupt.
The first draft is usually right in content and weak in motion. That is normal. This is where you come in.
Step four, feedback. Always give a time and a change. At zero thirty three, the transition is too slow, make it fast and sharp.
Name the motion too. Ease out, a hard hit, appear on the same beat as the logo. Specific words give specific fixes.
Expect several rounds. Each round fixes a few moments, and the result climbs every time.
Put the first draft next to the final one. Same content, but now it has impact and rhythm.
So the work moves from your hands to your eyes. Watch closely, write down the moment, say what to change, and repeat.
